# dtcloud_vm (Resource)

Manages a virtual machine.

`name`, `flavor_id`, `state` and `enable_hot_plug` change in place -- changing `flavor_id` resizes the machine, which stops it first unless hot plug is enabled. The `network` and `block_device` blocks and the boot-time arguments (`key_name`, `user_data`, `script`, `is_gpu_image`) all force replacement, because the API cannot change them on a live instance.

Interfaces and volumes can still be added after boot, but through `dtcloud_vm_network_interface` and `dtcloud_vm_volume_attachment` rather than by editing this resource's blocks.

No endpoint echoes the boot-time arguments back, so drift in them is invisible to Terraform. To build several machines, use Terraform's own `count` or `for_each`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_vm" "web" {
  name      = "web-01"
  flavor_id = data.dtcloud_flavors.small.flavors[0].id
  state     = "running"

  key_name  = dtcloud_ssh_key.deploy.name
  user_data = base64encode(file("${path.module}/cloud-init.yaml"))

  # Interfaces declared here are created with the machine and live and die with
  # it. Add one afterwards with dtcloud_vm_network_interface instead.
  network {
    uuid            = dtcloud_network.app.id
    security_groups = [dtcloud_security_group.web.id]

    fixed_ip {
      ip_version = 4
    }
  }

  # The boot disk is boot_index 0.
  block_device {
    boot_index            = 0
    volume_size           = 40
    source_type           = "image"
    device_type           = "disk"
    destination_type      = "volume"
    uuid                  = var.image_id
    volume_type           = "standard"
    delete_on_termination = true
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `block_device` (Block List, Min: 1) Block devices to attach at boot. The boot disk is the entry with boot_index 0. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--block_device))
- `flavor_id` (String) ID of the flavor (sizing). Changing this resizes the VM in place.
- `name` (String) Name of the virtual machine. Can be changed in place.
- `network` (Block List, Min: 1) Network interfaces to attach at boot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--network))

### Optional

- `enable_hot_plug` (Boolean) Allow live vCPU/memory resize on the instance. Can be toggled after creation.
- `graceful_shutdown` (Boolean) When stopping, ask the guest to shut down (softStop) instead of cutting power (hardStop).
- `is_gpu_image` (Boolean) Set when booting a GPU image.
- `key_name` (String) Name of an existing SSH key to inject, e.g. a dtcloud_ssh_key resource's name.
- `script` (Block List, Max: 1) Initial credentials applied to the guest at first boot. On a Linux image, set username, hostname and disable_root as well — they are optional only because Windows template images ignore them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--script))
- `state` (String) Desired power state: running, stopped or shelved. Shelving releases compute resources while keeping the VM and its disks.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user_data` (String) Cloud-init user data.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the VM was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `flavor_name` (String) Human-readable name of the VM's flavor.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `image` (String) Name of the image the VM was built from.
- `image_os_type` (String) OS family of the image, e.g. linux or windows.
- `last_modified` (String) When the VM was last modified, in RFC 3339 format.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Metadata the platform attaches to the instance, e.g. ha_enabled.
- `network_interface` (List of Object) Network interfaces currently attached to the VM. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_interface))
- `primary_ip` (String) Convenience shortcut: the primary IP of the first public interface, falling back to the first interface with an address.
- `ram` (String) Memory as reported by the API, e.g. "512 MB".
- `ssh_key` (String) Name of the SSH key injected into the VM.
- `status` (String) Current power/provisioning state, e.g. ACTIVE, SHUTOFF, ERROR.
- `task_state` (String) In-flight OpenStack task, empty when the VM is settled.
- `vcpus` (Number) Number of virtual CPUs.
- `volume` (List of Object) Volumes currently attached to the VM, including the boot disk. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volume))

<a id="nestedblock--block_device"></a>
### Nested Schema for `block_device`

Required:

- `boot_index` (Number) Boot order. The boot disk is 0.
- `delete_on_termination` (Boolean) Whether the device is deleted with the VM.
- `destination_type` (String) One of: volume, local.
- `device_type` (String) One of: cdrom, disk.
- `source_type` (String) Where the device comes from. One of: blank, image, volume, backup.
- `volume_size` (Number) Size in GB (1-8192).
- `volume_type` (String) Storage policy / volume type the disk is created on.

Optional:

- `uuid` (String) ID of the source image, volume or backup. Omitted for blank devices.


<a id="nestedblock--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Required:

- `fixed_ip` (Block List, Min: 1) Fixed IPs to request on this interface. At least one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--network--fixed_ip))
- `security_groups` (List of String) Security group IDs bound to this interface. At least one is required.
- `uuid` (String) ID of the network to attach to.

Optional:

- `port_security_enabled` (Boolean) Whether port security (and therefore security groups) applies to this interface.

<a id="nestedblock--network--fixed_ip"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network.fixed_ip`

Optional:

- `ip_address` (String) Specific address to request. Allocated by the platform when omitted.
- `ip_version` (Number) IP version, 4 or 6.



<a id="nestedblock--script"></a>
### Nested Schema for `script`

Required:

- `os` (String) Guest OS family. One of: linux, windows.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Initial password for the guest account.

Optional:

- `disable_root` (Boolean) Disable direct root login. Required in practice on Linux images; ignored by Windows template images.
- `hostname` (String) Hostname to set inside the guest. Required in practice on Linux images; ignored by Windows template images.
- `username` (String) Account to create. Required in practice on Linux images; ignored by Windows template images.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

Read-Only:

- `is_public` (Boolean)
- `mac_address` (String)
- `network_id` (String)
- `network_name` (String)
- `port_id` (String)
- `primary_ip` (String)
- `secondary_ips` (List of String)
- `security_groups` (List of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedobjatt--network_interface--security_groups))
- `spoofing_protection` (Boolean)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The boot-time arguments (key_name, user_data, script, is_gpu_image) are not
# reported by any endpoint, so an imported machine takes them from the
# configuration rather than from the platform.
terraform import dtcloud_vm.web 4c9a1f37-8d25-4e60-b13f-6a7c2e5b9d88
```
